notes: Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme (LKCSP) is a donor-funded undergraduate merit scholarship at Singapore Management University (confirmed on https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/financial-aid/lee-kong-chian-scholars-programme: 'Made possible by a generous gift from the Lee Foundation, the Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme (LKCSP) is one of our most prestigious scholarships...'). It is a Bachelor's degree merit award administered for scholar development by SMU's Student Success Centre / Centre for Scholars' Development; it is not a research degree, so no supervising professor or faculty supervisor is attached to the award. Professors list is empty by design (no supervision role exists for this scholarship type).

notes: SUTD PhD President's Graduate Fellowship (PGF) is tenable for PhD studies at SUTD (official page: https://www.sutd.edu.sg/admissions/graduate/scholarship/sutd-graduate-fellowships-scholarships). The SUTD PhD Programme overview (https://www.sutd.edu.sg/programme-listing/sutd-phd-programme/) states: 'Access to multiple world-class faculty with co-supervision flexibility' and that 'Potential applicants who are interested in the SUTD PhD Programme... may identify SUTD faculty member(s) whose research focus are closely aligned to their research areas of interest', with faculty listed per pillar (ASD, EPD, ESD, HASS, ISTD, SMT). The three professors above are SUTD faculty (verified email addresses published on their official SUTD profile pages) selected as representative potential PhD supervisors across SMT, ESD and ISTD; general PhD admissions enquiries go to phd@sutd.edu.sg. Max 3 professors recorded per batch rules; the full faculty list (187 members) is at https://www.sutd.edu.sg/about/people/faculty/.

QUAD STEM Scholarship Scheme is a Government of India undergraduate scholarship administered centrally by ICCR via the A2A portal (official_source_url: https://a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in/scheme/quad-stem-scholarship), funded by the Ministry of External Affairs. It covers B.Tech study at eight designated Indian institutes; no supervising professor or faculty is attached to the scheme itself (supervision, if any, is determined per admitted student at the host institute after selection). The A2A portal pages are JavaScript-rendered and returned no static content on fetch, but the scheme attaches no supervisors regardless, so no professors are recorded. Outcome: not_applicable per central-government-scheme rule.

Dr. S. Radhakrishnan Cultural Exchange Scholarship Scheme is a Government of India cultural-exchange scholarship administered centrally by ICCR via the A2A portal (official_source_url: https://a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in/scheme/radhakrishnan-cultural-exchange) for UG, PG and PhD study at Indian universities. As a central scheme it attaches no named supervising professors; supervisors depend on the host university assigned after selection. The A2A portal is JavaScript-rendered and returned no static content on fetch, but no supervisors are attached to the scheme regardless. Outcome: not_applicable per central-government-scheme rule.

India Science and Research Fellowship (ISRF) is a DST-funded visiting research fellowship implemented by INSA (official ISRF brochure: https://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/ISRF-Brochure-2025-26.pdf; programme page: https://insaindia.res.in/scientific/). Fellows work 3-6 months at 'premier research laboratories and academic institutions in India'; the brochure states 'The Academy will assist the researchers in identifying the host institution wherever necessary' and candidates finalize dates with their host Indian scientist. No professor/host scientist is attached to the scheme itself; scheme contacts are administrative (Dr Brajesh Pandey, Executive Director, INSA, isrf.dst@insa.nic.in; DST contact Dr Charu Agarwal, c.agarwal@gov.in). Outcome: not_applicable per central-government-scheme rule.

UGC Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Research Associateship (RA) for Foreign Nationals is a Government of India statutory-body scheme (UGC, https://www.ugc.gov.in) tenable at Indian universities generally; no supervising professor or faculty is attached to the scheme. Outcome: not_applicable per central-government-scheme rule.

TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme is centrally administered by UNESCO-TWAS and CSIR (official page: https://twas.org/opportunity/twas-csir-postgraduate-fellowship-programme). Fellowships are 'tenable in CSIR research laboratories and institutes in India' (a network of 38 institutes) and applicants must obtain acceptance from a chosen host CSIR institution; the page names only programme officers (TWAS Fellowships Office, fellowships@twas.org; Dr (Mrs) Mamta Sharma, CSIR ISTAD, mamtasharma@csir.res.in), not supervising professors. Outcome: not_applicable per central-scheme rule.
